- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in recent days), model often overshoots and forecasts too high; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, model frequently fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slightly (1–3%) in the 2nd half of the 30-day window.  
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment > 0.05 for 3+ consecutive days.  
- Forecast often lags true price by 2–5 days in the first 10 days — adjust early forecast by +0.5–1.0% to align with sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ sentiment-adjusted values.
